input.message: A streaming protocol keeps parallel tool calls apart primarily through unique identifiers attached to every message chunk. When a model issues multiple tool invocations concurrently, each call is assigned a distinct ID at the moment it opens, and every subsequent delta—arguments, partial JSON, or output tokens—carries that same ID as a tag. The client-side parser demultiplexes the incoming stream by grouping chunks according to their ID rather than their arrival order, allowing interleaved fragments from different calls to be reassembled correctly even though bytes from separate calls may physically interleave on the wire. Explicit start and end events bound each call's lifecycle, so consumers know when a given tool call's argument stream is complete and ready to execute, independent of how other concurrent calls are progressing.
